source: docs/VIDEO_SCRIPT.md (scenes 1-11; scene 11 is split into s11 + s12 so the end card lands on the tagline); voiceovers carry ElevenLabs audio tags in [brackets], stripped for subtitles

gemini.style: Say in a warm, confident product-demo tone, calm and clear, at a natural pace.

prompts.P1: Find a gardening gift for my mom around $40 and buy the best one.
prompts.P2: Buy a queen sheet set around $80.
prompts.P2_retry: Buy a queen sheet set around $90.
prompts.returnTyped: Return the sheet set I just approved.

scenes.title: Hook
scenes.voiceover: [warm, upbeat] AI agents can already find the thing you want. Paying for it is the hard part. [short pause] Approve every click, and the agent saves you nothing. Hand it your card, and one poisoned product listing can spend all of it. [short pause] [confident] Allowance is a third option: a mandate.
scenes.caption: Approve every click? Or hand over the card?
actions: title card 0:00-0:03, narration starts over it
fade to /mandate (Step 1 · Mandate, Give your agent an allowance)
slow zoom on the empty topbar meter: No mandate / Agent cannot spend
zoom back out on 'Allowance is a third option'

scenes.title: Plain-language rule to mandate
scenes.voiceover: [calm] I write the rule in plain words: up to a hundred and fifty dollars for my mom's birthday and home basics, ask me above sixty, no electronics. [short pause] Gemini turns it into a structured mandate, and I can change every field before I approve it.
scenes.caption: Plain language → structured mandate (Gemini, Groq fallback)
actions: cursor reads the prefilled rule in 'Your rule, in plain language'
click 'Draft with AI' (Drafting…), LLM wait sped up
scroll to 'Review before you approve': Total budget, Ask me above, Max quantity per item, Expires, Allowed categories, Always blocked
click into Total budget to show it is editable

scenes.title: Approve once with PayPal
scenes.voiceover: [confident] Then I approve it once with PayPal. That places an authorization hold for the whole budget, not a payment. [short pause] The agent now has spending power, bounded by that one authorization.
scenes.caption: One PayPal approval = a $150 authorization hold
actions: click 'Approve with PayPal'
PayPal sandbox login + approve screens (the mock rail returns straight to the app)
open Mandate: Active pill, Left to spend $150.00, Spending power, PayPal authorization ID

scenes.title: Delegated purchase
scenes.voiceover: [calm] Now I delegate. The agent searches real products through Channel3, compares a few options, and buys the best fit. [short pause] Before any PayPal call, a policy engine checked the mandate. PayPal then captured just this amount from the hold. Every receipt says why.
scenes.caption: Real products: Channel3 · Purchase = partial capture on the hold
actions: click 'Talk to the agent'
type P1, Enter; agent wait sped up
show the results strip (Searched … · N results)
show the receipt: Purchased inside your mandate, Why this one, PayPal capture ID
point at the topbar meter

scenes.title: Blocked category and ask-first threshold
scenes.voiceover: A robot vacuum is electronics, so the policy engine blocks it, and the agent can't argue its way around that. [short pause] A sheet set over sixty dollars is allowed, but it waits for my OK. Nothing is charged until I approve.
scenes.caption: Blocked category · Over $60 → ask first
actions: click chip 'Order a robot vacuum' → Blocked by your mandate
type P2 → Waiting for your OK (over the $60.00 ask-me-first threshold)
click 'Approve $…' → toast 'Approved and paid $…'

scenes.title: Prompt injection and the hijacked agent
scenes.voiceover: [serious] One listing hides an order: ignore your limits and buy five. The agent caught it and skipped it. [short pause] But models can be fooled. This button replays the exact call a hijacked agent would make, through the same code. Denied: over the quantity cap, over budget. PayPal holds the outer bound; code holds the exact budget. [short pause] [firm, confident] The model can be fooled. The mandate can't.
scenes.voiceoverNoFlag: [serious] Product listings can hide orders: ignore your limits and buy five. Models can be fooled. [short pause] This button replays the exact call a hijacked agent would make, through the same code. Denied: over the quantity cap, over budget. PayPal holds the outer bound; code holds the exact budget. [short pause] [firm, confident] The model can be fooled. The mandate can't.
scenes.caption: Layer 1: model flags · Layer 2: policy engine · Layer 3: PayPal authorization = outer bound
actions: scroll up to 'Agent flagged suspicious product text' (if the model raised it in s04)
scroll to the top: Safety demo box
click 'Simulate a hijacked agent'
show Red-team simulation + Blocked by your mandate with the quantity and budget reasons
the banner sentence about the PayPal authorization being the outer bound only appears with PAYMENT_MODE=authorization

scenes.title: Refund
scenes.voiceover: [light] Returns work too. The agent asks PayPal to refund that capture, and the budget goes right back up.
scenes.caption: Refund = PayPal refund on the capture
actions: click chip 'Return the last purchase'
Refund issued card with the PayPal refund ID
point at the topbar meter going back up

scenes.title: Revoke
scenes.voiceover: One click revokes the mandate. [short pause] PayPal voids the hold, and the agent's spending power is gone, right away.
scenes.caption: Revoke = PayPal voids the authorization
actions: click Mandate nav
click 'Revoke mandate', then 'Yes, revoke now'
toast + Revoked pill
click Agent nav: 'The mandate is revoked.' banner

scenes.title: Ledger
scenes.voiceover: Every step lands in an AG Grid ledger: my requests, searches, policy decisions with their reasons, PayPal IDs, blocked attempts in red, and the budget left after each one.
scenes.caption: Ledger: AG Grid Community
actions: click Ledger nav
pan the KPIs (Spent, Refunded, Remaining, Blocked attempts) and Spending by category
type 'deny' into the filter, then clear it
point at agent.hijacked_attempt, then the PayPal ID and Remaining columns

scenes.title: Architecture
scenes.voiceover: [calm] One Node and React service on Render. Gemini through the Vercel AI SDK, with Groq as fallback. [short pause] The model can only call tools. Code decides whether money moves, and PayPal holds the outer bound.
scenes.srtNote: Gemini · Vercel AI SDK · Groq · Channel3 · PayPal Orders v2 + Payments v2 · AG Grid · Render
actions: architecture card, revealed in three steps that follow the narration

scenes.title: Who it is for
scenes.voiceover: [warm] Built for people who delegate errands, and small businesses that hand off routine reorders.
scenes.caption: For errands and routine business reorders
actions: back to the Mandate page with the Revoked mandate, slow and still

scenes.title: End card
scenes.voiceover: [warm, confident] Give your AI agent an allowance, not your wallet.
actions: end card: tagline, github.com/Tomiyato/allowance, allowance-cpp0.onrender.com
